title: Stabilize variant affinity and fallback coordination after capacity surge
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed a regional capacity surge in the eu-west pool that triggered a cascade of routing decisions: autoscaler reactions, KV-cache evictions, and non-deterministic variant tie-breaks. The net effect was a short-lived window where requests were routed to incompatible model variants (wrong quant/architecture), followed by rapid cross-region reroutes that created an oscillation and elevated latency for several high-throughput tenants.

Timeline & detection: The incident began at 2026-03-08T02:12Z when the eu-west autoscaler signaled a scale-up due to a burst from a few customers. A telemetry spike in prefix-miss and kv-eviction-rate was visible at 02:16Z. By 02:18Z router traces show policy_version mismatches between regional controllers; the router's tie-break logic used a stale variant affinity hash and chose incompatible variants for a subset of requests. Cross-region reroutes started at 02:19Z and peaked at 02:22Z; mitigations reduced the noise by 02:40Z.

Root cause: Three contributing factors:
1) Metric lag in capacity reporting -- autoscaler scaled based on delayed utilization metrics which led to overprovisioning and then rapid eviction of cached keys when the pool rebalanced.
2) Router tie-break non-determinism -- the policy evaluation path used a non-monotonic tie-breaker (entropy-based) that could pick a variant using a stale policy_version when controller snapshots were not yet propagated.
3) Fallback coordination gap -- the fallback policy allowed cross-region variant substitution without verifying compatibility (quantization/sequence length), producing wrong-variant responses and triggering client-level retries which amplified the load.

Immediate mitigations already applied:
- Disabled cross-region fallback for eu-west at 02:30Z (short-term kill-switch).
- Increased policy snapshot propagation frequency from 15s to 5s for affected shards (temporary).
- Reverted aggressive autoscaler window to a conservative smoothing config to prevent oscillatory scaling.

Action items (owner — target):
- Implement deterministic variant affinity resolution (router): ensure variant selection is stable across controller snapshots; include monotonic policy_version check before accepting a variant (owner: Marcel Nguyen — target: 2026-03-18). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/5421
- Add variant compatibility check in fallback path (router + model metadata): reject fallback to variant that fails a compatibility fingerprint (owner: Priya Rao — target: 2026-03-16). Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/5440
- Harden autoscaler smoothing and add circuit-breaker to avoid near-term re-evictions (owner: Luis Moreno — target: 2026-03-17). Proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Autoscaler+Smoothing+Proposal
- Telemetry and traces: emit policy_version, variant_hash, kv_eviction_count per request and add dashboards/alerts for cross-region reroute rate > 1% baseline (owner: Elena Park — target: 2026-03-15). Datadog board: https://app.datadog.com/board/xyz-routing
- Post-incident QA: run a chaos test that simulates delayed policy propagation and cache eviction to validate behavioral guards (owner: SRE team — target: 2026-03-25). Test plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/chaos-routing

Acceptance criteria:
- No regression of client-facing errors attributed to wrong-variant selection in the next 4 weeks.
- Cross-region reroute rate should be below 0.1% for production traffic after rollout.
- Dashboards and an automated alert (pager) for reroute oscillation and variant-mismatch are in place.

Notes & links:
- Incident timeline and raw traces: https://incident.redwood.ai/INC-2026-03-08-routing
- Postmortem doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Variant+Affinity+Incident+2026-03-08
- Related prior work: ENG-24106 (variant resolution deadlock), ENG-101555 (regional policy loop resilience).
